rationale:
Evidence: the best design so far (iteration 2, score 391.8) finishes the oval reliably (20/20, mean 939 points, 1.98 s) but leaves the line on the s-bend (progress 0.37) and slalom (progress 0.19). Every failing run ends off_track with max_error about 0.063 m, just past the 0.06 m limit. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which is 0.06 m for any body width up to about 0.19 m, so it cannot be widened. Steering oscillation is low (0.19 to 0.22 on the failing tracks), so the robot is not jittering. It is lagging behind the bends and drifting out. Line loss is 0.25 to 1.0 events, which means the sensor array only loses the line after the robot is already far off. Sensing range is not the main limit. Iteration 2 also lowered base_speed (1.3 to 1.1) and s-bend progress fell from 0.58 to 0.37, so slowing down alone does not fix the bends.

Changes: (1) kp 5.0 to 6.0 for stronger correction on tight bends, where the robot currently lags. (2) kd 0.6 to 0.8 to damp the larger correction, since oscillation is low and there is room to add damping. (3) ki 0.0 to 0.3. The contract describes a fixed left/right motor mismatch, which produces a steady drift to one side that proportional control alone must hold against. A small integral term can cancel it. The integral is limited to +/-2, so windup is bounded. (4) base_speed, geometry, sensor weights and line_loss are unchanged, so the effect of the gain changes can be read directly.

Expected result: max_error below 0.055 on s-bend and slalom, slalom progress above 0.5, s-bend completion possible. Oval completion should hold, with completion_time staying near 2.0 s. Hypotheses: H1, higher kp reduces the lag-driven drift on tight bends. H2, ki removes the steady bias from the motor mismatch, lowering rms_error on straights. H3, kd 0.8 keeps the stiffer loop from oscillating. Next measurements: completion and progress per track (did the s-bend and slalom finish), max_error and rms_error (is the bias removed), steering_oscillation (is kp 6 with kd 0.8 too stiff), and completion_time (cost of the stiffer loop).
